heroHeadline: PLA Sorties Surge to 28/Day (24 Crossing Median Line) on Sep 18 — Window High for Crossings — as Jioupeng Drill Closes with First Drone-Integrated Live-Fire and a Chinese Recon Drone Shadowing Lai's Inspection; Premier Launches Taiwan-Matsu No. 4 Subsea Cable; MAC Reaffirms US First-Island-Chain Commitment Ahead of Sept 24 Trump-Xi Summit; Beijing Had Warned It Could Cancel That Summit Over a Pending US Arms Sale (Sep 13)
heroSubtitle: Since our last full update (Aug 27), PLA gray-zone pressure has climbed for five straight days into and through Taiwan's own live-fire drill. Daily median-line crossings rose from 2 (Sep 14) to 7 (Sep 15) to 12 (Sep 16) to 17 (Sep 17) before hitting 24 of 28 sorties on Sep 18 — the most crossings recorded in a single day since the Sep 7 surge (29 sorties, 17 crossing) and just short of that all-time non-exercise sortie count. The escalation coincided with Taiwan's three-day joint precision-strike drill at Jioupeng Base in Pingtung (Sep 16-18), which tested HIMARS, Hsiung Feng III, Tien Kung III and, for the first time, integrated attack drones (ALTIUS-600M, Switchblade) into joint combat scenarios; President Lai inspected the final day as a Chinese reconnaissance drone flew from the southwestern Strait to waters off Taitung overnight to monitor the exercise, prompting Taiwan to scramble aircraft, ships and coastal missile systems in response. Away from the drill, Premier Cho Jung-tai inaugurated the NT$1.4 billion Taiwan-Matsu No. 4 subsea cable on Sep 18 as a communications-resilience backstop for the outlying islands, and Mainland Affairs Council Deputy Minister Shen Yu-chung said Taipei continues to receive assurances that Washington remains committed to deterrence along the first island chain, pushing back on warnings from former NSC chief Su Chi about weakening US resolve ahead of President Trump's Sept 24 meeting with Xi Jinping. That summit has its own shadow over Taiwan: Beijing warned on Sep 13 it could cancel the meeting if Washington approves a pending $14 billion Taiwan arms package beforehand, restating the Taiwan question as a 'red line' in bilateral relations. Earlier in the period, President Lai promulgated the KMT/TPP-authored drone-industry funding act (Sep 11) resolving the Aug 27 budget standoff, NSC Secretary-General Joseph Wu publicly rejected an Atlantic magazine feature questioning Taiwan's will to resist China (Sep 10), and TSMC reported a fourth straight record month — August revenue of NT$514.8 billion, +53.3% YoY — as AI chip demand continued to outstrip supply (Sep 10).
